To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
containers are not yet ready for NFV, but they have the potential to become the building block of the future NFV platform.

(1) containers are not yet suitable for high-performance network applications, and (2) the main reason is that containers do not support hardware offload of packet processing, and (3) the main reason for that is the lack of support for hardware offloading in the Linux network stack.
the throughput of container-based network functions can be improved by up to ≈ 2.5 times with the help of a new approach called network function container.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of containers in NFV, and we propose to address the performance issue with a container-based NFV platform that can achieve 10Gbps throughput
the performance of the container-based NFV platform.

the following three aspects: (1) how to deploy NFV on container-based platform with high performance and low overhead; (2) how to design and implement a NFV platform with low latency, high packet processing throughput, and low overhead; and (3) how to design a NFV platform to support the deployment of multiple network functions with low overhead.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current container-based NFV is not ready yet for high-performance applications.
containers are not ready yet for the deployment of high-performance NFV.
the performance of container-based NFV is not satisfactory yet, and there are many considerations for deploying high-performance container based NFV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance bottleneck of the container-based NFV platform is the network interface.
we can achieve ≈ 3.4Mpps with containers on the same hardware, and the overhead of the container is less than 10%.
containers are a good fit for NFV, but the current performance is not enough.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the throughput of container-based NFV is still far from the throughput of bare metal NFV.
the performance of container-based NFV platform is limited by the containerization technology, not by hardware.
container-based NFV is a viable alternative to virtual machine based NFV.
